title: CASE and HAVING: labels and group filters

steps.title: CASE: if-this-then-that labels
steps.prompt:
CASE makes a new column from rules, like a price tag sticker: 'pricey' or 'ok'.
WHEN the rule fits, THEN the value; ELSE is the fallback; END closes it.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT name, price, CASE WHEN price > 300 THEN 'pricey' ELSE 'ok' END AS tag FROM products;
hints: SELECT name, price, then the CASE.
ELSE 'ok' covers the rest, END finishes.
Write the compact CASE expression and alias it AS tag.
steps.expected_sql: SELECT name, price, CASE WHEN price > 300 THEN 'pricey' ELSE 'ok' END AS tag FROM products;
steps.memory_trick: CASE = 'decide as you go, row by row'.

steps.title: Fill the CASE elbow
steps.prompt:
Fill the blank so expensive products get the 'luxury' label:
SELECT name, CASE WHEN price > 1000 THEN 'luxury' ___ 'standard' END FROM products;
steps.task: Fill the blank with the else-word.
hints: The else-case word is four letters.
It sits between the two labels.
steps.expected_sql: SELECT name, CASE WHEN price > 1000 THEN 'luxury' ELSE 'standard' END FROM products;
steps.seed_sql: SELECT name, CASE WHEN price > 1000 THEN 'luxury' ___ 'standard' END FROM products;
steps.memory_trick: WHEN … THEN … ELSE … END - the full decision recipe.

steps.title: HAVING: a WHERE for piles
steps.prompt:
WHERE filters ROWS. HAVING filters PILES (groups).
Find the categories with more than five products.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT category_id, count(*) AS c FROM products GROUP BY category_id HAVING c > 5;
hints: Build the GROUP BY query first.
count(*) AS c gives the count a name.
Write the GROUP BY … HAVING query.
steps.expected_sql: SELECT category_id, count(*) AS c FROM products GROUP BY category_id HAVING c > 5;
steps.memory_trick: HAVING = the WHERE of the GROUP BY world.

steps.title: Predict the pile filter
steps.prompt:
This query piles products by category, then keeps only the big piles:
SELECT category_id, count(*) FROM products GROUP BY category_id HAVING count(*) > 5;
Product counts per category_id are: 8, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 3, 4.
With HAVING count(*) > 5, only ONE pile survives.
hints: Only one pile has more than 5 products - it has 8.
steps.memory_trick: HAVING shaves the chart to the tall bars.
